summary.headline: APAR Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 26.7% YoY to INR6,603 crores; PAT of INR254 crores was INR285 crores before INR31 crores of one-offs.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR6,603 crores, with domestic sales up 33.6% and exports up 13.3% YoY. Reported PAT of INR254 crores (3.8% margin) included about INR31 crores of one-offs (gratuity/leave encashment, ECB mark-to-market, and a legal provision); management says the operating PAT was about INR285 crores, up around 14%. FY26 revenue was INR22,902 crores (+23.3%), EBITDA INR2,067 crores (9% margin) and PAT INR977 crores (4.3% margin). Management flagged a near-term slowdown from the Middle East war, metal and freight cost spikes, polymer shortages and project deferrals, while reiterating medium-term growth and raising FY27 capex to about INR1,500 crores.

segments.name: Conductor
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR3,764 crores (+29.9% YoY); EBITDA INR44,919/MT vs INR41,430 a year ago; premium products 49.3% of revenue. FY26 revenue INR12,712 crores (+32.7%), crossing INR10,000 crores, EBITDA INR43,012/MT vs INR36,683; order book INR7,671 crores at March 31; order inflow INR11,450 crores in FY26.

segments.name: Oil (specialty and transformer oil)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue up 5.6% YoY with volumes roughly flat; EBITDA INR5,656/KL vs INR5,873/KL, including about INR15 crores of forex provision. Exports were 36.3% of Q4 revenue vs 41.7%. FY26 revenue INR5,373 crores (+6%), EBITDA INR5,943/KL vs INR6,145/KL. Domestic transformer oil +12.2% for FY26.

segments.name: Cables
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,903 crores (+35% YoY); EBITDA INR202 crores at 10.6% margin (+34.5%). FY26 revenue INR6,220 crores (+25.8%), EBITDA INR633 crores at 10.2% margin; cables overtook oil as the second-largest segment. Order book about INR1,800 crores.

guidance_outlook: Conductor medium-to-long-term EBITDA guided at INR35,000-36,000/MT plus tailwinds; no explicit FY27 guidance given.
Cable volumes targeted to grow about 25% a year; conductor volumes about 10% a year.
FY27 capex about INR1,500 crores (Conductor ~INR400 crores, Cables ~INR850 crores, Oil ~INR200 crores), on top of INR740 crores spent in FY26.
Management expects a short-term slowdown in orders and deliveries across India and the US, with US business to grow in FY27 and further in FY28 under Section 232 tariffs.
Middle East business expected to stay subdued until the war is resolved; Iraq conductor deliveries pushed out.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation: Conductor about 90-95%, Cables about 85-90%, Oil about 65-70%; lubricant small-can and bucket filling at 85-90%, with debottlenecking capex planned.

Cable capex is building toward the INR10,000 crore revenue goal, with about INR400 crores spent in FY26 and about INR850 crores carried into FY27; spend is being pulled forward by about INR400 crores.
Cable expansion covers medium-voltage XLP and EPR/rubber cables for data centres, plus wind, solar, railways and defence.
Conductor is at 5 expansion phases; exports of CTC have started to Middle East manufacturers, with Europe and US approvals in progress.
Management says the capex cycle has lengthened from order to installation.
demand_pricing: Conductor order book INR7,671 crores at March 31; premium products are over 50% of the current order book, versus 45.8% of FY26 revenue.
US demand is led by data centres: about $15 million of cables supplied to 3 data-centre projects so far; US cable revenue rose 52.2% YoY in Q4 and 46.7% for FY26.
Section 232 duty is 25% on copper and aluminium cables and 50% on aluminium conductors, which management sees as giving landed-cost visibility.
Domestic HVDC transformer oil awards have just been made; conductor and oil supply for these projects is expected to come later, running through FY27-FY28.
Competition: domestic players are adding capacity, pressuring prices; UltraTech and Adani are seen as focused on building and light-duty wires, while APAR focuses on specialty cables.
Specialty polymer prices and availability were hit by the Middle East war, which limits near-term specialty cable order booking and will hurt volumes and margins.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the US data-centre opportunity, and how should FY27-28 US growth and the capex be read?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects strong US traction led by data centres, with RFQs rising and US demand for both cables and conductors growing; a larger US presence is expected in FY27. Management also said it is not seeing hyperscaler capacity blocking of the kind seen in fibre.

qa_highlights.question: How should FY27 conductor profitability be thought of?
qa_highlights.answer: Medium-to-long-term conductor EBITDA is guided at INR35,000-36,000/MT plus tailwinds; the company does not give next-year guidance and will update as visibility improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and the breakup of the INR1,500 crore FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is Conductor 90-95%, Cables 85-90%, Oil 65-70%. FY27 capex splits into about INR400 crores Conductor, INR200 crores Oil and INR850 crores Cables.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dependence on the Middle East for specialty oils, sourcing and sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Sourcing from Saudi Aramco's Yanbu refinery has continued without interruption. Shipments to Saudi Arabia and Kuwait stopped in March and April and resumed in May at higher freight; the Middle East business is expected to stay subdued until the war ends.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for premium conductor volumes and CTC exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium conductors were 45.8% of FY26 revenue and over 50% of the order book. CTC exports to Middle East manufacturers have started, with Europe and US approvals in progress.

qa_highlights.question: Will the capex raise cable volumes, and does domestic competition affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is fungible across specifications, and the capex is pulling forward spend toward the INR10,000 crore cable target. Management said new entrants may cost a few percentage points of EBITDA, but the market is growing.

risks_watch: Metal price spikes: aluminium at the SHFE premium of about $330-360/t and higher MJP premium, plus freight and insurance cost increases from the war.
Project deferrals and delivery delays from labour shortages around state elections and port disruptions; customers are postponing deliveries.
Polymer supply and price shock affecting specialty cable volumes and margins in the near term.
Competitive pressure from domestic capacity additions and new entrants (UltraTech, Adani, a private player seeking PGCIL approval for a conductor technology).
Forex and ECB mark-to-market exposure; INR15 crores forex provision in oil in March.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term growth runway and US and data-centre demand, but explicitly cautious on the next two to three quarters because of war-related metal, freight and polymer costs and project delays. Management declined to give FY27 conductor guidance and pointed to medium-term ranges instead.
key_quotes: So if you exclude these non -operating impacts which are amounting to INR31 crores, the PAT which came in at INR254 crores would have been at INR285 crores.
We plan to increase our capex for FY27 to about INR1,500 crores in addition to the FY26 capex that we have incurred of INR740 crores.
So we see the cable side on the data center growing and being a larger opportunity for APAR as time passes by.
